Use a volume view to present the user with a slider control for setting the system audio output volume, and a button for choosing the audio output route when the option is available.
To instead display a volume slider as an alert, use the functions described in .
Sliders are always displayed as horizontal bars and an indicator, or thumb , notes the current value of the slider, which the user can move to change the setting.
The system draws the region between the thumb and the end of the track associated with the slider’s minimum value using the minimum volume slider image .

Use animated artwork to highlight unique aspects of your content and provide a more immersive experience for people who use your app.
Animated artwork consists of a video asset for the animated artwork itself and a static preview image which should ideally match the first frame of the video.
Use the key appropriate for the aspect ratio of your animated artwork within : Provide animated artwork for either, neither, or both of these keys, depending on the available formats for your media.
Aim to use the same between media items if the animated artwork doesn’t change; for example, the album artwork for songs within an album is constant.
When the system requires a preview image, it uses the for the currently-provided (for the required animated artwork variant).
Ensure the aspect ratio of any preview images or video assets you provide matches the aspect ratio indicated by the animated artwork key you associate the with.
Avoid high frame rate video (greater than 60 fps), as the system may not display your animated artwork.
